PR:ADDRESS                       	Gerhard C. Hildebrandt, MD, Room no. CC401A, Ben Roach Building, Markey Cancer

PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is a potentially
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	curative treatment option for a variety of hematological malignancies.
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	Interactions between the donor immune system and the patient tissue result in a
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	disease, called GVHD. The pathophysiology of acute GVHD can be hypothesized in
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	three sequential phases: cytokine storm and activation of the antigen-presenting
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	cells (APC), donor T cell activation and effector cell phase. Idiopathic
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	pneumonia syndrome (IPS) is one of the most deleterious complications after
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	allogeneic HCT and is considered not only to be related to conditioning regimen
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	toxicity but also represents an end organ damage caused by allo-reactive T
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	cells, therefore making the lung susceptible to a two-pronged attack, one of
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	which overlaps with GVHD causing other target organ injury. IPS results in
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	mortality of up to 90% of patients. We will use a murine model of IPS and GVHD
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	which is well established in our group, and in which disease evolves either
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	across disparities in major histocompatibility complex (MCH) class I and II,
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	minor histocompatibility antigens (miHags) or both. Metabolomics changes
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	following syngeneic and allogeneic HCT at post-transplantation Days +7 (cytokine
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	storm phase) and Days +42 (cellular effector phase) are compared to baseline
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	wild-type (naive) controls. Prior to analysis, naïve - and experimental mice
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	(N=3 from each group) were fed with semi-liquid diet supplemented with tracers
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	(13C6-glucose ) over 24 hours. At the end of 7 days or 42 days, respectively,
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	feces and aGVHD target organs (colon, liver and lung) were collected from all
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	groups and further processed and / or analyzed. We expect to reveal metabolic
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	pathways affected after allo-HCT which contribute to immune cell mediated lung
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	injury (IPS) and will potentially identify different metabolic pathways in other
PR:PROJECT_SUMMARY               	GVHD target organs.
PR:PROJECT_TITLE                 	Metabolomics of lung injury after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation

#MS
MS:INSTRUMENT_NAME               	Orbitrap Fusion
MS:INSTRUMENT_TYPE               	IC-FTMS
MS:ION_MODE                      	NEGATIVE
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	ICMS Analytical Experiment with detection of compounds by comparison to
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	standards.  Thermo RAW files are loaded into TraceFinder and peaks are manually
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	curated. The area under the chromatograms is then exported to an Excel file. The
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	area is then corrected for natural abundance. The natural abundance corrected
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	area is then used to calculate the concentration of each compound for each
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	sample. This calculation is done using standards. The first sample ran on the
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	ICMS is a standard that has known concentrations of certain compounds. Then a
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	number of samples are ran (typically 3-4) followed by another standard. The
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	equation to calculate the concentration is "intensity in sample"/("intensity in
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	first standard" + (("intensity in second standard" - "intensity in first
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	standard")/# of samples) * "known concentration in standard", where the
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	"intensity" is the aforementioned natural abundance corrected area, and the
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	unlabeled intensity from the standard is used for all isotopologues of the
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	compound. The reconstitution volume is simply the volume that the polar part of
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	the sample was reconstituted to before going into the ICMS. The injection volume
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	is how much of the reconstitution volume was injected into the ICMS. The protein
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	is how much protein was in the entire sample (not only the small portion that
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	was aliquoted for the ICMS). The polar split ratio is the fraction of the polar
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	part of the sample that was aliquoted for the ICMS. This is calculated by
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	dividing the weight of the polar aliquot for ICMS by the total weight of the
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	polar portion of the sample. The protein normalized concentration is calculated
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	using the equation, concentration * (reconstitution volume / 1000 / polar split
MS:MS_COMMENTS                   	ratio / protein).
MS:MS_TYPE                       	ESI
